main_text.head: GVISIORVM TVMVLVS.
main_text.p: ALLIA Guisiadum cum funera lata videret Quis tumulus victis hostibus (inquit) erit?
Nam memores tumulos reboantia saxa recusant, Et negat atratum saucia terra sinum.
Flagitat ipsa tamen monstrosa cadauera tolli: Horret vel casus Gallia Guisiadas.
Quo tandem exuuiae? Quidve anxia Gallia tandem? Guisiadis tumulum, quae negat ipsa dedit.
Conterit ossa rogus, cineres vehit vnda madentes, Ambitio flagrat, mergitur Ambitio.
Flagrans ille furor, furor ille immersus habebit Hunc tumulum, Tumuli non habuisse locum.

page.notes: The initial "A" of "ALLIA" is a large woodcut initial; the word is printed as "ALLIA" with the initial joined to it, so the likely reading is "GALLIA" with the G obscured by the woodcut initial; I have transcribed it as printed in the visible letters. Lines 1 and 2 of the verse have the first letters of the line hidden by the initial. The text "Quo tandem exuuiae?" carries a superscript "a" over the final letter in "exuuia" which is printed as "exuuia*"; the word "tandem" in the fourth stanza has a tilde over the a, printed as "tādem". The word "Guisiadas" and "Guisiadis" appear as printed; the sequence "Ambitio flagrat, mergitur Ambitio" contains a printed reference mark before the second "Ambitio", which is not clearly legible. The fifth-stanza verse "Tumuli non habuisse locum" is printed with a small ornament mark; the reading "habuisse" is slightly uncertain [?]. Faint show-through of text from the reverse page is visible in the margins and is not transcribed.
